brief: Goldman Sachs partner Bobby Molavi surveys the first eight months of 2026. Index returns are healthy and equities sit at the upper bounds of the top decile of returns since 1929, with heavy factor, sector and thematic rotation beneath the surface. He splits the questions into a big box (AI value creation and capex, rates and inflation, Iran/US and oil) and a little box (positioning, momentum, crowding, issuance, M&A, debasement). The chain he draws: Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole tilt puts a September hike back on the table if August CPI and PPI print firmer, the 10 year yield is ticking higher, and gold and bitcoin ripping alongside debasement search interest points to renewed US fiscal and dollar concern. Iran/US has no offramp, so oil stays sticky high, which presses inflation and the consumer. Nvidia's $96bn quarter and 2027 guidance of +70% against sell side estimates of +40 to 45% say AI capex is not going away. Positioning is cleaner, leverage and long/short ratios have come in, August flows felt jittery and defensive rather than risk on, and midterm year August to October seasonals are poor. He leaves AI ROI, the rates path and retail's effect on price discovery unresolved.
